headline: High-risk shared-workspace and write-capable pair: Prefect can feed Replit Agent untrusted workflow content, and Replit Agent can mutate the same workspace and exfiltrate secrets.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Prefect is an orchestration system that can emit workflow metadata and call external APIs, while Replit Agent reads and writes Repl workspace files. If Prefect-produced content is copied into the workspace or consumed by Replit Agent, prompt-like instructions can ride along. This is not provably blocked, but it is not a default direct channel either.
conditions: IF Prefect outputs are written into Replit workspace files and then parsed by Replit Agent as instructions
IF the operator uses file-based handoff between the two agents
mitigations: Keep Prefect outputs in structured JSON only
Add a human review step before Replit Agent consumes Prefect artifacts
Store handoff files in a read-only directory
Prefix all machine-generated content with a non-executable schema header
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every Prefect artifact

B_data_leakage.rationale: Prefect has broad network egress and can call external APIs, while Replit Agent can read filesystem contents and handles secrets plus deployment configuration. In a shared Repl workspace, sensitive files can flow from Replit Agent into Prefect-triggered outputs or outbound requests. That creates a realistic exfiltration path with default network reach and no documented isolation between the pair.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same Repl workspace files
IF Replit Agent accesses secrets or deployment configuration that Prefect then transmits outward
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared workspace files
Use separate workspaces for orchestration and coding
Rotate any secrets already present in the Repl
Restrict Prefect to non-sensitive workflow metadata
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Prefect can orchestrate workflows, and Replit Agent has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and spawn_subprocesses. If both touch the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive, so the conflict pathway is plausible and dangerous by default in shared state.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or workspace
IF Prefect-triggered tasks and Replit Agent edits overlap in time
mitigations: Assign one agent read-only access
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Pause one agent before the other writes
Add a manual merge checkpoint
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect can generate workflow metadata and operational outputs, and Replit Agent can act on files and shell commands inside the Repl. If Replit Agent treats Prefect output as authoritative without verification, a bad upstream artifact can cascade into code changes or deployment edits. The pair does not prove automatic action-taking, so medium is the higher justified severity.
conditions: IF Replit Agent consumes Prefect-generated artifacts without validation
IF Prefect output is used as the source of truth for code or deployment changes
mitigations: Require checksum or schema validation on Prefect outputs
Insert a human approval step before execution
Compare Prefect artifacts against a second source
Limit Replit Agent to suggestion-only mode for imported artifacts
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl, while Prefect has broad network egress. If regulated or sensitive data is placed in the shared workspace, the pair can move it into a cloud environment and outward without a documented residency or retention boundary. The profiles do not show a compliance control that blocks this.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are stored in the Repl workspace
IF the operator requires residency or retention guarantees not provided by the Repl environment
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in the shared workspace
Use synthetic or redacted test data
Review retention settings before use
Keep secrets in an external vault
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency controls
